meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, so let's start with who decided to give Owen a zero, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. That's one thing you've got right. Now tell me what you actually have on the essay.

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
That's 4.4, and nothing on his record is what I want in writing. But a rewrite of what, Hale? What is the concern, and what do you have behind it?
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
Okay. In writing, tonight, and I'll hold you to it. The zero is still in the gradebook, so what is it standing on?
So will you agree to the rewrite?
Not yet. If I take a rewrite now, I'm admitting something about Owen's essay, and I won't do that on a software score. What else do you have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that nothing will go on Owen's record, and you accepted that entering the zero before calling me broke procedure 4.2, but no rewrite was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, and I have seen no evidence that justifies it. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with the zero still on and no rewrite agreed, though you got a written promise of nothing on his record and she still wants the zero withdrawn and some evidence; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you did not get there because you showed her nothing to weigh.
What moved her: Owning in one sentence that you entered the zero before calling her gave you a small bit of ground, because it answered her procedure complaint without excuses.
What cost ground: Asking her to agree to the rewrite before you had shown any evidence, because accepting it then would have meant admitting something about Owen's essay.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; you never put anything about a particular night in front of her, so you were not close, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after owning the mistake about the zero, put one dated document about how Owen worked on the essay in front of her before you read her section 4.4.
